Kit

kit/interact

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Target discovery and command validationAPIWorked example: prompt and gate share the reach constantValidation limits and target selection

kit/interact helps select nearby chests, doors, or pickups for a use prompt and check interaction geometry when a command executes. It provides three procedures and one struct, with no engine types or action dispatch.

The procedures perform pure geometric checks and may run inside a simulation tick. The example below uses cooperative commands; simulation games can use the same checks in their commands and authority steps.

Target discovery and command validation#

Discovery selects the target to offer in the UI. Command validation decides whether an attempted interaction passes its geometric requirements:

  • Discovery runs on the client each frame. pick selects a nearby target from candidates the game collects from its registry.
  • Validation runs inside the command on the host. Call in_range/facing_ok with the same constants used for discovery.

Using the same procedures and constants keeps the client prompt and authority validation geometrically consistent. They can still evaluate different snapshots of a moving world; the authority's result is final.

Implement the action as a command on the target entity, such as opening a door or looting slot 2. kit/interact does not dispatch the command. See items.md for a loot command that applies these checks.

Positions use [3]f32: 2D games leave z at zero, while 3D games supply it. The API uses no engine types.

API#

Odin
Candidate :: struct {
	id:     u32, // knet.Net_Id-sized; kept engine- and package-free
	pos:    [3]f32,
	radius: f32, // per-target extra reach (a chest is easier to touch than a lever)
}

// Check distance against `reach` plus the target's radius. Uses squared
// distance without sqrt; suitable for commands and frame code.
in_range :: proc "contextless" (origin, target: [3]f32, reach: f32, radius: f32 = 0) -> bool

// Check the facing cone. `min_dot` expresses the cone half-angle as a
// dot-product threshold (0 = 180° cone, 0.5 = 120°, 0.7071 = 90°). A zero
// `facing` vector means omnidirectional; standing on the target always passes.
facing_ok :: proc "contextless" (origin, target, facing: [3]f32, min_dot: f32) -> bool

// The nearest candidate within reach and facing — what the prompt points at.
pick :: proc(cands: []Candidate, origin: [3]f32, reach: f32, facing := [3]f32{}, min_dot: f32 = 0) -> (best: Candidate, ok: bool)

Worked example: prompt and gate share the reach constant#

Declare one constant (examples/cavecrawl/scripts/cavecrawl.odin):

Odin
REACH :: f32(40) // interaction reach in pixels, shared by the prompt and host check

Discovery runs every frame in world.odin's update_prompt. The game collects candidates from its entity maps, then selects a target:

Odin
cands := make([dynamic]kinter.Candidate, context.temp_allocator)
for id, c in self.chests {
	append(&cands, kinter.Candidate{id = u32(id), pos = {c.x, c.y, 0}})
}
for id, d in self.doors {
	append(&cands, kinter.Candidate{id = u32(id), pos = {d.x, d.y, 0}})
}
best, ok := kinter.pick(cands[:], {me.x, me.y, 0}, REACH)

When ok is true, the game displays kit/ui prompt text such as "E — loot chest" or "E — open door" and retains best.id as the interaction target.

The predicted command in door.odin uses the same geometry and constant. Both the predicting client and the host execute the check:

Odin
@(gd_command = knet.ACTION_ANY_SEAT_PREDICTED)
door_toggle :: proc(self: ^Door, px: f32, py: f32) -> bool {
	if !kinter.in_range({px, py, 0}, {self.x, self.y, 0}, REACH) {return false}
	self.open = !self.open
	return true
}

The command carries the issuer's claimed position (px, py) as arguments; chest_take and pickup_grab use the same check. This validates distance from the supplied position; the geometry helper does not establish that the position is trustworthy. In host.odin, the host also uses kinter.in_range with REACH to check that the whole party is at an open door.

Validation limits and target selection#

  • Share the reach constant. The prompt and the host gate must use the same REACH and the same in_range check, or the UI may offer an interaction the host refuses, or hide one it would allow.
  • Position samples can represent different times. Choose REACH with expected movement delay in mind. When accepting client-supplied positions, validate them against host state, as combat does for cast origins.
  • facing = {} (the default) means omnidirectional; min_dot = 0 is a 180° cone, not "no cone". Standing exactly on the target always passes the facing check.
  • pick returns the nearest passing candidate. Per-target radius extends interaction range; selection still measures center-to-center distance.
  • Candidate collection is the game's job: walk your own entity maps into a temp_allocator array each frame, as update_prompt does.
